explanation: The divine Savior who heals the blind man and reveals himself as the light of the world.
The term for lack of physical sight, used here both literally regarding the man's condition and metaphorically regarding the spiritual blindness of the Pharisees.
A symbol of truth and God's presence that Jesus represents in contrast to the darkness of sin and unbelief.
The term for suffering or weakness, used here as an opportunity for God's works to be revealed through healing.
A group of religious leaders who in the story refuse to see the truth and judge the man based on their own traditions rather than the fact of the miracle.
